headline: Approved FY '27 school budget, 2026-2027 Valor High School handbook, and AP World Modern textbooks.
summary: The Waltham School Committee approved the Consent Agenda, the 2026-2027 Valor High School handbook with changes, AP World Modern textbooks, and the FY '27 School Department budget. The committee also discussed dual language space, CTE partnerships, the high school schedule, the District Growth Plan, and voted to pay bills on the FY '26 and FY '27 warrants.
decisions: Approved the Consent Agenda, including retirements, resignations, and minutes from June 17, 2026.
Approved the 2026-2027 Valor High School handbook with specified changes.
Approved the AP World Modern textbooks.
Voted to provide a copy of the Full Size Classroom Use document dated July 9, 2026 to the Waltham City Council for informational purposes.
Approved the FY '27 School Department budget as presented in the updated budget book.
Approved paying the bills on the FY '26 warrant.
Approved paying the bills on the FY '27 warrant.

 The School Committee reconvened at 6:03pm.  Present were Mr. Tarallo, Mr. Zanghi, 
 Mrs. Coleman, Mrs. AlJammal, Ms. DeJoannis, Ms. Wong-Bigelow, and Mayor 
 McCarthy.  Mayor McCarthy presided. 
 The Committee recited the Pledge of Allegiance. 
 Recent Waltham High graduate, Sierra Nicholas, addressed the Committee to 
 emphasize the importance of challenging high school students while they are in a 
 comfortable and supportive environment as it will provide them with a stronger 
 foundation in the future. 
 Waltham parent, Nicole Piche-Nicholas, voiced her concern with parents / caregivers 
 not being included in the high school schedule development process until the end. 
 Waltham parents, Jeff Korenstein, Jessica Powers, Maria Luiza Rodriguez, and Tom 
 Haley, also advocated for parent involvement and participation earlier in the high 
 school schedule process.  Parent Tricia Hurley expressed her concern with the 
 possible change from an eight period to a seven period schedule and the impact to 
 students, especially those on IEPs and in CTE programs. 
 There were no students present at the meeting.

 As previously requested, Dr. Mendonsa provided the members with a list of available 
 classroom space in stand-alone elementary schools across the district.  Dual 
 Language School was not included as it is in a shared building. 
 VOTED:  On motion of Mr. Tarallo, seconded by Mrs.  Coleman, to provide a copy of 
 the Full Size Classroom Use document dated July 9, 2026 to the Waltham City 
 Council for informational purposes.  All in favor. 
 A conversation between Ms. DeJoannis and Dr. Mendonsa ensued about maintaining 
 dedicated space for Fine and Performing Arts and science classes within our 
 schools. 
 The Committee received a list of the CTE Department’s partnerships with local 
 organizations and institutions, pursuant to a prior request. 
 Dr. Conley confirmed for Ms. DeJoannis that the intent is to continue to expand 
 opportunities for students by increasing the number of partnerships. 
 Mrs. AlJammal asked if all CTE students have the ability to participate in co-ops.  Dr. 
 Conley advised freshman and sophomores do not as they are early on in programs, 
 and opportunities for upper classmen in some of the newer programs are a work in 
 progress. 
 The superintendent confirmed the WHS Schedule Committee will meet later in July to 
 review the results of a recent staff survey and Dr. Conard will be taking over leading 
 this group. 
 Ms. DeJoannis asked that an analysis of available classroom space at the middle 
 school level be completed and information provided to the Committee, similar to that 
 of the elementary schools. 
 Mrs. Coleman provided a reminder of the superintendent’s evaluation process, 
 including important dates, to the members. 
 VOTED:  On motion of Ms. DeJoannis, seconded by Mr.  Tarallo, to take a recess at 
 6:49pm.  All in favor. 
 The Committee reconvened at 6:52pm with all members still present. 
 Dr. Mendonsa shared the Waltham Public School’s District Growth Plan for the 
 upcoming 2026-2027 school year.  She indicated the plan stemmed from a DESE 
 requirement for Waltham High School but was designed to help support the growth of 
 the entire district from preschool through high school.  Three priority goals were 
 shared: Equitable and Consistent Learning, Talent Development System and

 Welcoming Environments, along with standards and indicators.  Having clear 
 leadership and governance structure that advances equitable student outcomes 
 along with school leadership teams that monitor and improve teaching and learning 
 quality will be a focus. 
 In Curriculum and Instruction, ensuring multi-language learners and students 
 receiving disability services reach grade-level proficiency, improving literacy across 
 content areas through standards-based, culturally sustaining instruction, and 
 increasing proficiency in STEM-aligned content areas across the district will be the 
 department’s focus during the upcoming year. 
 The goals for Special Education and Student Services center around strengthening 
 home-school capacity so fewer students are transferred to outside placements, to 
 improve IEP quality, and establish sustainable quality infrastructure across the 
 department.  Additionally, there will be an emphasis on coherent and tiered support, 
 including strengthening interventions, for students in all schools. 
 Increasing access, making schools feel safer and more welcoming for students, 
 strengthening partnerships with BELPAC and SEPAC, and improving communication 
 and trust are the goals within Family and Community Engagement. 
 Human Resources will focus on publishing a multiyear workforce diversity strategic 
 plan, ensuring hiring and promotion practices are equitable and transparent, building 
 internal licensure pathways for staff, and supporting all educators from onboarding 
 through evaluation. 
 The goals of the Finance and Operations Department are to maintain a balanced 
 budget, implement a data-driven, equitable resource allocation model, establish 
 measurable operational efficiencies in facilities, transportation and procurement, and 
 secure funding for infrastructure and technology modernization. 
 Dr. Mendonsa explained how progress will be measured across all areas.  Members 
 asked some clarifying questions of Dr. Conley and Dr. Porch. 
 Mr. Tarallo, Ms. DeJoannis and Ms. Wong-Bigelow asked Mr. Mazza numerous 
 questions relative to the updated information for the approved FY ‘27 school 
 department budget.  The members requested a digital version of the finalized book 
 be provided to them and also be made available on the district’s website.
